subject: Issues with predicting into the Last Glacial Maximum

messages.author: 32a8d503caf9164e
messages.subject: Issues with predicting into the Last Glacial Maximum
parts:
Hello! 

I am trying to predict the distribution of the African leopard during the last glacial maximum. I run the model using current climatic data and then transfer to the last glacial maximum using CHELSA palaeo-climate data. At the moment I am just using bioclimatic variables but intend to include NDVI and surface ruggedness at a later stage. However, the predictions are extremely inaccurate (see photo attached). I have no idea why it could be making these predictions. Note, red is presence and the rest is considered absence. 

If anyone has tried to run such model and has encountered the same or similar issue, any assistance or advice would be so greatly appreciated!

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Issues with predicting into the Last Glacial Maximum
parts:
This is not the first time I've seen issues with projections. Can you tell me specifically which variables you are using for Envs and which for Transfer? If you tell me specifics, I can take a further look.
First, you can try downloading your session code RMD and run the analysis in R to see if you are getting the same results as within the Wallace GUI. 
Some other suggestions are to run a MESS analysis (the last module in the Transfer component) to see how much variation in past climate to what the model was built on, and then take a look into whether the model was clamped or not. Choosing either could affect your results if you're projecting into environmental conditions not found in the model training.

Bethany
The Wallace team
